key_insight: CORNETO’s ability to infer robust biological networks varies across distinct regimes shaped by available data and prior knowledge. Its reusability also depends on regularization and biological context.
problem_solved: Determining when a multi-omics network inference framework can be reliably reused across datasets and biological settings.
method: Study the reusability of CORNETO, an existing framework for learning biological networks from multi-sample, multi-omics data.
Assess how data availability, prior knowledge and regularization influence inference robustness.
Examine how biological context affects the conditions under which the framework remains reliable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this study highlights that successful reuse requires checking data coverage, prior assumptions and regularization—not simply transferring a model unchanged. Reliability should be evaluated in the target biological setting.
visual_elements: Conceptual regime map with data availability and prior knowledge as axes, illustrating differing robustness conditions.
Pipeline diagram: multi-sample omics data plus prior knowledge → CORNETO → inferred biological network.
Regularization dial beside a network graphic to illustrate its role in shaping inferred connections.
Side-by-side biological-context panels emphasizing that reliability can change across settings.
paper_title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
paper_authors: Xabier Martínez-de-Morentin, Sumeer A. Khan, Itziar Cenzano, Robert Lehmann, Alberto Maillo
